STEP 1 (scope read + design-space placement)

GOAL: fix an in-scope coupling position that is not one of the already-tried ones.
READ: workspace listing (only progress.jsonl exists, no repo code available); the scope contract, experiment policy and the round history in the task text.
OBSERVED (from task text): earlier accepted/probed ideas occupy these loci -- codeword re-positioning by Fréchet/Karcher/mass (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS), per-level curvature control from prefix-transition scores (CURVCTRL-SID), radial/entropy-ranked assignment (BRad-RQ), successor-profile smoothing and geodesic shift/boost (LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, succboost-geoshift), behaviour cones (behcone-prefix-rq), tangent-space graph SIDs (TSG-SID).
REASONING: the untouched loci are (a) the METRIC in which the residual quantizer measures its residual, and (b) the prefix composition rule. Both can carry behaviour and both are curved. Chosen position: a per-item determinant-one warp of the hyperbolic chord used at EVERY RQ level, with Möbius-addition prefix composition. Codeword parameters, curvature and codebook init stay exactly as in the baseline, so this cannot be read as a re-run of the Fréchet/Karcher or per-level-curvature ideas.
OPEN: whether the warp can be made implementable with no new tunable constant (all constants derived from measured quantities or documented defaults).

STEP 2 (constant-derivation check)

GOAL: make sure the mechanism needs no sweep and no ablation run to make its case.
READ: the binding experiment policy (no sweep, no ablation arm, no multi-seed, one run decides).
OBSERVED / DERIVED: the warp strength needs no free weight. alpha_i = lambda_1 / trace(M_i) is a measured quantity (dominant successor-direction share), s_i,k = exp(0.5*alpha_i*(log lambda_k - mean_k log lambda)) has prod_k s_i,k = 1 exactly (det W_i = 1, volume preserving, so the warp cannot cheat by shrinking the ball); clip s_i,k to [1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d)] is dimension-derived; the successor set S_i = smallest set covering 80% of the item's outgoing transition mass is derived, not chosen; the eigenvalue floor eps = 1e-6*mean(lambda) is scale-relative; c = 1 unit ball and r_max = 1-1e-3 are documented defaults; the commitment weight reuses the baseline's own value so no new loss constant is introduced.
REASONING: every number entering the mechanism is either measured, dimension/scale relative, or a documented default; nothing is selected by trying values. Removing behaviour sets W_i = I; removing geometry replaces the warped Poincaré chord by the warped Euclidean chord and Möbius addition by addition -- both switches exist in code, neither is trained in this round.
OPEN: cost at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs) - to be estimated next.

STEP 3 (cost at frozen scale)

GOAL: quantify per-step cost at 24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs.
READ: arithmetic done directly (no code available); assume baseline latent width d=32, SID length L=3, codebook size 256 per level, batch = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items/step.
OBSERVED / ESTIMATED: extra forward work per step = L * batch * 256 * (d^2 + 2d) = 3*1023*256*1088 ~ 0.86 GFLOP (the warp is one d x d matvec per (item, codeword) pair); with the backward pass roughly 2.0-2.5 GFLOP/step. Baseline nearest-codeword assignment is ~0.05 GFLOP/step, so the assignment is ~17x its old cost but assignment is a small fraction of the encoder forward/backward; net Stage-2 epoch time estimated +10-20%. Frame refresh once per epoch = one batched eigh of 24556 32x32 matrices (~30 ms on GPU) plus the sparse successor gather, i.e. <= ~5 min over 3000 epochs (<1% of Stage-2 wall clock). Stage-3 cost unchanged (the SID table is frozen before Stage 3).
REASONING: 72k steps * 2.5 GFLOP = ~180 TFLOP of extra work, minutes on four cards; the proposal is affordable inside the frozen budget. Implementation note: precompute B_i, s_i, and W_i per epoch and gather them per batch to avoid per-step eigh.
OPEN: nothing blocking; final block to be written.

IDEA: succframe-warp-rq
TITLE: Successor-frame warped Poincare quantization: one determinant-one behaviour metric shared by every RQ level
MOTIVATION: The RQ-VAE spends prefix resolution in directions that are convenient for item-content reconstruction, not in the directions in which users actually move. For a generative recommender this is a direct loss: two items that a user routinely moves between can land in different level-1 or level-2 prefixes, so the generator cannot condition the next prefix on the current one. The problem is not where the codewords sit but the metric in which each level measures its residual.
NOVELTY: Codeword parameters, curvature, codebook initialisation and codebook updates are left exactly as in the baseline; what changes is the metric of the residual quantizer. Each item gets a determinant-one linear reparametrisation W_i of the hyperbolic chord, built from its training successor second moment in the tangent space at the origin, and the same W_i is applied at every level so it shapes the whole prefix hierarchy at once. Earlier mechanisms here re-positioned codewords (Fréchet / Karcher / mass-weighted), set a per-level curvature (CURVCTRL), set radial position from transition entropy (BRad), smoothed successor profiles in Lorentz coordinates, or imposed behaviour cones; none warps the curved distance that selects codewords, and none derives the warp strength from the dominant eigenvalue share of the successor second moment.
CHANGE: Every level's nearest-codeword rule and every level's reconstruction/commitment term use the warped Poincare distance d^W(z, p_{l-1} (+) u) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) * || W_i ( (-z) (+) (p_{l-1} (+) u) ) ||) with W_i = B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T taken from the eigendecomposition of the item's successor second moment M_i = sum_j pi_ij t_j t_j^T; the prefix itself is composed by Mobius addition, p_l = p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k_l}.
SPECIFICATION:
(1) Offline, once per Stage-2 epoch, no gradient: A = directed adjacent-transition count matrix over training sequences only (item at position t -> item at t+1), 24556 x 24556 sparse. z = exp_0^c(clip(E_content, ||.|| <= R)) from the current encoder, detached; t = log_0^c(z). For each item i: S_i = smallest successor set covering >= 0.8 of i's outgoing transition mass; pi_ij = A_ij / sum_{j in S_i} A_ij. If |S_i| < 2 or mass 0: B_i = I_d, s_i = 1 (cold/uninformative fallback). Else M_i = sum_{j in S_i} pi_ij t_j t_j^T (uncentred, so both the mean successor direction and its spread enter), eigh -> lambda desc, B_i; lambda <- max(lambda, 1e-6*mean(lambda) + 1e-12); alpha_i = lambda_1 / sum_k lambda_k; s_i = exp( 0.5*alpha_i*(log lambda - mean_k log lambda) ), clipped to [1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d)]; W_i = B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T (det = 1).
(2) Quantization step, levels l = 1..L: p_0 = 0. For each k compute ch_k = (-z_i) (+) ( p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k} ); q_k = W_i ch_k; if ||q_k|| > r_max rescale to r_max; d_{l,i,k} = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh( sqrt(c) ||q_k|| ). k_l = argmin_k d, straight-through; u_{l,k_l} becomes the level-l SID token; p_l = clip_ball( p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k_l} ).
(3) Loss = sum_l d_{l,i,k_l}^2 + beta * commitment (beta and the codebook/EMA settings exactly the baseline's, no new loss constant). Codebook entries are kept inside the ball by post-step projection to radius <= 0.9; W_i is detached so no gradient flows through the frame.
COST: +10-20% Stage-2 epoch time at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs). Per step: 1023 items x 3 levels x

256 codewords x one d x d matvec (d=32) ~ 0.86 GFLOP forward, ~2.5 GFLOP with backward, versus ~0.05 GFLOP for the baseline assignment; assignment is a small share of the encoder step. One batched 24556-way 32x32 eigh per epoch (~30 ms GPU) plus a sparse successor gather, <= ~5 min over the whole of Stage 2. Stage-3 cost unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: successor structure in the training transition graph is predictive of next-item, and in the Poincare ball the successor directions are not the content-reconstruction directions. If true, the single coupled run gives Stage-3 test Recall@10 > 0.065, and, measured on the trained model alone, training transition pairs (i->j) share the level-1 and level-2 prefix at a higher rate than the same frozen encoder's codes produce under the identity frame (post-hoc re-assignment, no extra training). If Recall lands at or below the identity-frame expectation, the successor second moment is not the right frame and the idea is dropped.
RISKS: (i) alpha_i * eigenvalue spread may over-concentrate prefix resolution into a few successor directions and damage pure reconstruction, so codes stop covering the catalogue; (ii) the 0.8-mass successor sets can be tiny (1-2 items) and noisy for tail items, giving near-degenerate frames; (iii) per-epoch frame refresh makes the metric non-stationary, which can prevent the codebooks from settling; (iv) warping the chord can push ||q|| toward 1, where artanh gradients explode; (v) successor information may already be captured by Stage 3's sequence model, leaving only reconstruction damage; (vi) computing a second (identity-frame) assignment for the diagnostic adds code paths that could silently diverge from the trained one.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: directed item transitions, i.e. the per-item successor distribution over training sequences.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: adjacent pairs (item_t, item_{t+1}) counted over all training-split user sequences only, aggregated into a sparse 24556 x 24556 count matrix A; pi_ij normalised over the smallest successor set covering 0.8 of each item's outgoing mass; success items projected through the current (detached) encoder to tangent coordinates t_j at the origin. Recomputed once per epoch, no gradient.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: transitions and successor sets come only from the Stage-2 training split, over the 24556 training items; validation and test interactions are never read, so no user in validation/test contributes an edge, and no validation/test item can appear as a successor. The SID table is frozen before Stage 3 and Stage 3 trains and is evaluated without any further SID update, so no test statistic can re-enter the code construction; the identity-frame diagnostic uses only training transition pairs.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: fixed negative curvature Poincare ball with c = 1 (unit ball, r_max = 1 - 1e-3), with exp/log maps at the origin, Mobius addition (+) and subtraction, the hyperbolic distance (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||.||), and a determinant-one linear warp W_i applied to the chord before the artanh. Curvature is fixed, not trainable.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: inside the RQ-VAE residual quantizer of Stage 2, at every level l = 1..L: codeword selection, the per-level reconstruction/commitment term, and the prefix composition p_l = p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k_l}. Not in the item encoder and not in Stage 3.
COUPLING PATH: one pathway: the training successor distribution -> successor second moment in the ball's tangent space -> det-1 warp W_i -> the warped Poincare chor

d -> nearest-codeword index at level l -> the level-l SID token -> Mobius composition of the prefix -> the loss gradient on the encoder and the codebooks -> next epoch's frames. Removing the behaviour sets W_i = I and the pathway collapses to plain hyperbolic RQ; removing the geometry replaces the warped Poincare chord with a warped Euclidean chord and the Mobius prefix with plain addition, so neither term can be dropped without changing the selection that produces the SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: d_{l,i,k} = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c) * || W_i [ (-z_i) (+) ( p_{l-1,i} (+) u_{l,k} ) ] || ), with W_i = B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T, M_i = sum_{j in S_i} pi_ij t_j t_j^T = B_i diag(lambda) B_i^T, s_i,k = exp(0.5 * alpha_i * (log lambda_k - mean log lambda)), alpha_i = lambda_1 / sum lambda; behaviour enters through pi_ij and alpha_i, curvature through (+), (-) and artanh, and both meet inside the same norm that selects the codeword.
OBSERVABLES: per-level codeword usage histograms and the number of used codewords; the distribution of alpha_i and of s_max/s_min; successor prefix-agreement rate at level 1 and level 2 over training transition pairs for the trained SID versus the same encoder under the identity frame; prefix-transition predictability of the generator (accuracy of predicting level-l token of the next item from the current item's level-l prefix); Stage-3 test Recall@10 against the 0.065 bar; and the gradient norm contributed by the warped term to the encoder.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: identical code with W_i = I_d for every item (no successor second moment, no alpha, no eigenbasis); everything else, including Mobius prefix composition and the Poincare chord, unchanged. Switch exists and is exercised only by unit tests in this round, not trained.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: identical code with the curved terms replaced: chord measured in flat coordinates, d = || W_i( z_i - (p_{l-1} + u_{l,k}) ) ||^2, and the prefix composed by plain vector addition; the behaviour warp W_i stays. Switch exists, not trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full coupled run described above: successor-frame warp W_i inside the warped Poincare chord, with Mobius prefix composition, trained once, no sweep, no extra seed.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
epoch hook (no grad):
  A <- transitions(training sequences); t_i <- log_0^c(z_i) with z_i = exp_0^c(clip(f(e_i), R)), detached
  for each i: S_i <- min set covering 0.8 * out_mass(i); pi_i <- normalise(A_i,S_i)
     M_i <- sum_{j in S_i} pi_ij t_j t_j^T ; (lambda, B_i) <- eigh_desc(M_i)
     lambda <- max(lambda, 1e-6*mean(lambda)+1e-12); alpha_i <- lambda_1/sum(lambda)
     s_i <- clip( exp( 0.5*alpha_i*(log lambda - mean(log lambda)) ), 1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d) )
     W_i <- B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T          # det = 1
  fallback: |S_i| < 2 or out_mass(i)=0 -> W_i <- I_d
step hook (levels l = 1..L):
  p_0 <- 0
  ch_{i,k} <- mobius_add( mobius_neg(z_i), mobius_add(p_{l-1,i}, u_{l,k}) )
  q_{i,k} <- W_i ch_{i,k};  q <- q * min(1, r_max/ (||q||+1e-12))
  d_{i,k} <- (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c)*||q_{i,k}|| )   # arg clipped to 1-1e-7
  k_l <- argmin_k d ; token_l <- k_l ; p_{l,i} <- clip_ball( mobius_add(p_{l-1,i}, u_{l,k_l}), r_max )
  loss <- sum_{l} d_{i,k_l}^2  + beta * commitment(codebook, p_{l-1} side)  # beta = baseline value
  straight-through gradient from p_{l,i} to encoder latent; W_i detached
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: inputs per item: content embedding e_i, prefix point p_{l-1,i} in the ball, level-l codebook U_l inside the ball, and the precomputed fram

e (B_i, s_i) or equivalently W_i. Outputs per item per level: the chosen index k_l and hence the level-l SID token, the new prefix point p_{l,i} in the ball, and the scalar warped Poincare distance used in the loss. Episode-level outputs: the SID table (item -> (token_1,...,token_L)) consumed by Stage 3, plus the recorded frames and distances.
SAFEGUARDS: Mobius arithmetic in the algebraically stable form with the denominator floored at 1e-8; every achieved point re-projected to ||p|| <= r_max = 1-1e-3 after each addition and each codebook update; the chord rescaled if the warp pushes it past r_max; artanh argument clipped to 1-1e-7 and implemented as 0.5*log((1+x)/(1-x)); eigenvalue floor relative to the measured trace; s_i clipped to [1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d)] so det(W) = 1 and no direction is annihilated; alpha_i clipped to [0,1]; frames detached and refreshed only once per epoch to avoid chasing a moving encoder; identity fallback for items with fewer than two successors or zero outgoing mass; the identity-frame diagnostic re-uses the same distance function object as the trained path so the two cannot diverge; NaN/Inf guard on the per-level loss with the step skipped and logged if triggered.
END IDEA
